story.iWant: to drag clips from media library to the timeline
story.soThat: I can arrange my video sequence
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Create Timeline container component (AC: #1) - Create Timeline.tsx in src/renderer/components/Timeline/ - Render as fixed-height horizontal strip at bottom of layout - Style with Tailwind: dark background, border-top - Subscribe to timelineStore.clips and timelineStore.tracks - Integrate into MainLayout component
- Task 2: Create timeline data store (AC: #5, #7) - Create timelineStore.ts in src/renderer/store/ - Define Clip and Track interfaces (see Data Model below) - Implement actions: addClip, removeClip, updateClip, setPlayhead - Initialize with single track (Track 1) and playhead at 0 - Export store hook: useTimelineStore
- Task 3: Implement drop zone for timeline (AC: #2) - Add onDragOver and onDrop handlers to Timeline component - Extract file ID from event.dataTransfer.getData('fileId') - Look up full MediaFile from mediaStore using file ID - Calculate drop position on timeline based on mouse X coordinate - Call timelineStore.addClip() with clip data
- Task 4: Create TimelineClip component (AC: #3, #4) - Create TimelineClip.tsx in src/renderer/components/Timeline/ - Display clip thumbnail strip (multiple frames or single thumbnail) - Display clip duration using formatTime() utility - Position based on clip.startTime (pixels from left) - Width based on clip.duration scaled by zoom level - Style with Tailwind: rounded, border, hover effect
- Task 5: Create timeline ruler with time markers (AC: #4) - Create TimelineRuler.tsx component - Render horizontal ruler above track with time labels - Display markers at regular intervals (0:00, 0:10, 0:20, etc.) - Sync ruler scale with timeline zoom level - Style with monospace font for time labels
- Task 6: Create Playhead component (AC: #7) - Create Playhead.tsx component - Render vertical line indicator at timelineStore.playheadPosition - Position using CSS transform based on playhead time and zoom - Style with distinct color (cyan or red) and full-height - Initially positioned at 0:00 (left edge)
- Task 7: Implement auto-zoom to fit clips (AC: #6) - Calculate total timeline duration from all clips - Compute zoom scale: timelineWidth / totalDuration - Apply zoom to clip widths and ruler scale - Ensure minimum zoom level (clips not too narrow) - Will be refined in Story 4.2 (manual zoom controls)
- Task 8: Handle sequential clip placement (AC: #5) - When adding clip, calculate next available position - If timeline empty, place at 0:00 - If clips exist, place after last clip (end of last clip's duration) - Update clip.startTime to sequential position - Prevent clip overlap (will be relaxed in multi-track Story 4.1)
- Task 9: Create TimelineTrack component (AC: #1) - Create TimelineTrack.tsx component - Render track container with clips positioned inside - Handle track-specific drop events - Display track label ("Track 1") on left side - Style with border, fixed height (e.g., 80px)
- Task 10: Write unit tests - Test Timeline component renders tracks and clips - Test timelineStore.addClip() updates state correctly - Test clip positioning based on startTime and duration - Test auto-zoom calculation with various clip counts - Test sequential placement logic prevents overlap

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Timeline renders as horizontal track at bottom of screen 2. User can drag clip from media library to timeline 3. Dropped clip appears on timeline with thumbnail strip 4. Clip shows duration and position on timeline ruler (time markers) 5. Multiple clips can be placed sequentially on timeline 6. Timeline automatically adjusts zoom to fit all clips initially 7. Playhead indicator visible at timeline start (position 0:00)

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: FR005: Application shall provide a visual timeline interface showing imported clips with playhead/scrubber. FR007: Synchronize playhead position between timeline and preview player. Timeline UI shall maintain 30+ fps responsiveness with 10 or more clips loaded (NFR001).

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: Bottom: Timeline with playhead, zoom controls, and basic editing tools (split, trim, delete). High contrast for playhead and selected clips. Simple, functional UI that can be built within 72-hour sprint.

doc.title: Architecture Documentation
doc.snippet: Zustand 5.0.8 for global state management. Minimal boilerplate, excellent TypeScript support, perfect for 72-hour timeline. Store creation pattern: create with clips, tracks, playheadPosition state.

doc.title: Architecture Documentation
doc.snippet: Track contains clips array. Clip interface: id (UUID), sourceFile (absolute path), startTime (position in seconds), duration (seconds), trimIn/trimOut offsets, trackId. TimelineState manages tracks array, playheadPosition, totalDuration (computed), zoomLevel (pixels per second), selectedClipId.

doc.title: Architecture Documentation
doc.snippet: Timeline component folder structure: Timeline.tsx (main container), TimelineTrack.tsx (individual track), TimelineClip.tsx (clip display), Playhead.tsx (playhead indicator), ZoomControls.tsx, timeline.types.ts. Store at src/renderer/store/timelineStore.ts.

doc.title: Architecture Documentation
doc.snippet: Render only visible clips (virtual scrolling if greater than 50 clips). Use CSS transforms for playhead movement (GPU accelerated). Store time as seconds (number), file paths as absolute paths.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: Goal: Enable video import and create functional timeline with playback controls. Deliverable: User can import videos, see them in media library, drag to timeline, and play in preview. Story 2.4 builds on Story 2.3 (media library with drag source).

doc.title: Story 2.3: Media Library Display
doc.snippet: MediaItem has draggable="true". onDragStart handler stores file ID in event.dataTransfer.setData('fileId', id). Integrates with Timeline drop handler in Story 2.4.

constraints.constraint: Must use Zustand for state management - create timelineStore.ts following same pattern as mediaStore.ts (lines 30-66)
Must use Tailwind for all styling - no separate CSS files (per architecture.md)
Must return JSX with React.JSX.Element type annotation (per existing component pattern)
Time values stored as seconds (number type), not milliseconds
File paths stored as absolute paths (string type) matching MediaFile.path format
All components must have JSDoc block comments describing purpose
Maximum file size: 500 lines per file (per CLAUDE.md)
Functional programming pattern - use function keyword for pure functions, avoid classes
Dark theme color scheme: zinc-900 background, zinc-700/800 borders, cyan-500 accents
Timeline must maintain 30+ fps responsiveness per NFR001
Single track for MVP (trackId: 1) - multi-track deferred to Story 4.1
Clips positioned using CSS left/width with zoom scaling, not canvas rendering

interface.name: MediaFile
interface.signature: interface MediaFile { id: string; path: string; name: string; format: string; duration: number; resolution: { width: number; height: number }; size: number; thumbnail?: string; createdAt: number }

interface.name: useMediaStore
interface.signature: useMediaStore(): { files: MediaFile[]; isImporting: boolean; selectedFileId: string | null; addFile(file: MediaFile): void; selectFile(id: string | null): void; ... }

interface.name: DragEvent.dataTransfer
interface.signature: event.dataTransfer.getData('fileId'): string - retrieves MediaFile.id set by MediaItem during drag start

tests.standards:
The project uses Vitest 4.0.4 as the testing framework with React Testing Library 16.3.0 for component testing. Test setup is configured in src/renderer/src/__tests__/setup.ts which mocks window.api and window.electron for IPC communication tests. Testing patterns observed:
**Store Tests (Zustand):** - Use describe/it/expect from Vitest - Reset store state with useStore.setState() in beforeEach - Test state initialization, actions, and state mutations - Reference acceptance criteria in test descriptions (e.g., "AC: #4") - Use getState() to access current store state directly
**Component Tests (React):** - Use render() from @testing-library/react - Use screen queries (getByText, getByRole) for element selection - Test rendering, props, user interactions, and layout structure - Verify Tailwind classes applied correctly - Use toBeInTheDocument() and class matchers
**File Naming:** [FileName].test.tsx for components, [storeName].test.ts for stores, placed in __tests__ subdirectory adjacent to source files.
**Coverage Focus:** Unit tests for logic and state management. Manual testing for media operations per ADR-008.
